title: Baked red cabbage and chickpea fritters

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Tinned chickpeas, eggs, flour, yoghurt and fresh vegetables are all plain kitchen staples with nothing factory-made.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item on Tesco shelves at a normal price.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a bowl, a masher and a roasting tray, and spooning out fritters is simple.

works.reason: Two tins of chickpeas bound with two eggs and 50g flour make 12 fritters, a fair lunch for four, and 25 minutes at 220°C is enough to crisp them and soften finely shredded cabbage.

honest_times.reason: Shredding cabbage, slicing spring onions, mashing, shaping 12 fritters and making the dip fits in 20 minutes, and the bake matches the 25 minutes printed.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including all 3 tbsp of oil, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Red cabbage is in season in early September, and 300g of it gives the fritters their colour and title, so it is the point of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Chickpea and vegetable fritters with yoghurt and salad make a filling, wholesome lunch that a family would happily eat again.
